text:
sam: Quick follow-up to the on-prem packaging RFC — proposing a small compatibility layer between the agent and package transport. Want to lock down the upgrade contract (negotiation, migration steps, rollback guarantees) before next sprint.

maria: Agree. Can you sketch the contract boundaries? I want to know what the agent must implement vs packager.

sam: Sketch: handshake with schema version, supported capabilities, and a declarative "apply plan" that the agent executes idempotently. Packager produces a signed artifact + metadata. Agent decides whether to stream or stage.

lee: Important: we have constrained devices with <1GB disk. Full image swaps aren't acceptable. Need patch/overlay support + compaction; also consider in-place migration risk.

anita: Proposal: three-layer contract: 1) manifest schema + semver, 2) transport handshake (chunked signed blobs), 3) apply API with checkpoints + health probe. Agent should expose /apply-start, /apply-status, /apply-commit, /apply-rollback endpoints.

ben: +1. Also need a migration mode for older agents: if packager sees an agent that only understands v1, packager should emit a compatibility bundle (legacy shim) or mark the artifact as operator-assisted. No automatic destructive migrations without operator opt-in.

sam: Exactly. For manifest versioning I propose using semver-style major bumps for breaking schema changes. Packagers must include a "supported_agent_min" field and an "operator_instructions" blob for human-assisted steps. Example manifest snippet: 

```json
{"manifest_version":"2.0.0","supported_agent_min":"1.3.0","components":["service","config"],"apply_plan":"plan-uuid-1234"}
```

maria: How do we ensure atomicity if agent crashes mid-apply? Checkpointing + copy-on-write? We should avoid orphaned state that requires manual fixes.

lee: Agent will stage into a new directory, run health checks on the staged service, then switch a symlink atomically. Rollback simply switches symlink back and restarts service. For low-disk targets we can stream a patch directly into the running process where supported (restart with -patch flag).

anita: Need explicit semantics for "staged" vs "stream" apply modes. Staged = verify checksums, run preflight, promote. Stream = best-effort patching with conservative safety checks. Both must emit pre/post checksums and a commit token.

ben: Also: define failure modes and idempotency. /apply-start returns a plan-id. If agent reboots mid-plan, client can query /apply-status and resume or rollback by plan-id. Packager signs the plan so agent can verify integrity.

sam: Telemetry hooks: pre+post checksums, final state, exit code, duration. For private deployments telemetry should be optionless and only send minimal success/failure + hash to control-plane; detailed logs live on customer side.

maria: Operator API requirements: dry-run, force-rollback, and a "compat-suggestion" field in packager output if agent is too old. That suggestion can include a link to operator steps or a path for staged upgrade.

lee: We should also specify an on-disk layout migration contract: migration scripts must be reversible, idempotent, and limited in scope. If a migration is irreversible, packager must mark it and make it operator-assisted.

anita: Security: all manifests and plan objects signed with our artifact key. Agent should validate signatures and reject plans if the manifest_version > agent_major and no compat shim available.

ben: Operational note: for resource-limited hosts add a "scratch_limit" manifest hint so agent can refuse staging if it would OOM/disk-full. Packager can then fall back to operator-assisted mode.

sam: OK I'll update the RFC draft with sections: contract boundaries, handshake example, /apply endpoint defs, failure semantics, telemetry/privacy, and operator workflows. Who can review the patch? cc @maria @lee @anita.

maria: I'll take endpoint defs and request/response shapes.

lee: I'll prototype the symlink + health probe flow on a tiny VM.

anita: I'll draft telemetry and privacy notes for Private deployments.

ben: I'll write compatibility guidelines for packagers and the "compat-suggestion" template.

upgrade-bot: scheduled: RFC-compat-layer update PR opened by sam at https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/482 :rocket:

sam: Thanks team. We'll sync next Tue in arch sync if needed. :thumbsup:
